title: A smooth point of a fibre maps to the smooth locus of a flat morphism
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For $y\in Y$, let $w\in X_y$ be a point of the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. If $X_y\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ is smooth at $w$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], then $f$ is smooth at the image of $w$ in $X$. Smoothness at a point means membership in the open smooth locus, or equivalently existence of an open neighbourhood on which the morphism is smooth.

source.place: Tag 01V9, lemma-smooth-at-point, (2) implies (1); already proved as Scheme.Hom.fiberι_mem_smoothLocus in lean/WeilConjectures/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/SmoothFiber.lean:154-202.

proof.text: Apply the pointwise flat-fibre criterion [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion] at the image x of w. The fibre inclusion is injective and identifies w with the canonical fibre point over x; global flatness implies flatness on its stalk. The smooth fibre neighbourhood therefore gives a smooth neighbourhood of x. The attached source-library theorem already proves this implication directly: choose affine neighbourhoods whose fibre lies in the smooth fibre locus, apply the flat smooth-fibre algebra criterion, and transfer membership in the smooth locus along the affine open isomorphisms.
